The whole text is re-parsed on every commit and on every source-editor analysis; there is no incremental parsing. Measured 2026-11-18 in Node 24 on Windows 10 (wasm64, median of 10 warm runs, parse and hash): specs/exegra (788 KB) 243 ms through the Lean kernel against 35 ms for the JavaScript it replaced; specs/benchmark (134 KB) 67 ms against 9 ms. Of the 243 ms about 95 ms is Exegra.Json.parse reading the request (WG-4797), 27 ms the derivation, 10 ms reference resolution, 33 ms the hash and 45 ms writing the reply. In Chromium (Playwright, tests/browser/lean-core.spec.js) the same parse and hash take 312 ms (median of 7).

tasks.detail: Known unknown of Normal form and hash.
tasks.title: The key-order theorem assumes distinct keys in every object; the derivation produces such values (it assigns members like JavaScript), but that is not itself stated as a theorem yet.

Hierarchies, cuts and facets are declared and queried (cutMap, blockOf, cutToCut, facetMembers, knowledgeOf); quotients over cuts and level-aware claims use them (semantic-abstraction), but views that adopt a declared cut are WG-5695.
Module elements are derived from the declared implementation.modules, not extracted from the code, so the module-to-element map is only as true as those declarations (WG-5696).

Hierarchy, cut and facet well-formedness is checked in JavaScript (validate.js and query.js); the Lean derivation accepts the sections as data but does not check them, and laminar families and cut maps have no Lean definitions or theorems yet (WG-5699).
History, undo and redo stacks are unbounded in memory and are not persisted: undo is lost on reload and per CLI invocation.

Only operation transactions and replacement sources are validated before they commit. Undo and redo restore text that was committed before and do not validate again, and reload commits any text that parses, so the model after a reload can carry validation errors.
The session never passes expectRevision or expectHash; only the CLI uses the optimistic checks (--expect-hash).

A deletion or a rename re-derives the model of the current text before it plans its edits, because references and expressions of entities edited earlier in the transaction are known only to a derivation: about 2.6 s each on a 7 MB specification (WG-4980).

The validation of a transaction's result is a full validation: rule and example results are not cached per entity (WG-4974). Measured on a 7 MB specification, validation is about 0.9 s of a single-property apply; the model derivation is about 2.6 s.
Behavioral results hold for the listed scenario traces only; there is no exhaustive state-space exploration and no probabilistic evaluation.

Claim evaluation runs on the caller's thread. In the application session.evaluate runs it on the main thread inside every semantic commit, and trace and metric claims run engine scenarios there (src/core/claims.js), unlike the Simulation tab, which runs its scenario in the engine worker. The cost on large models is not measured (WG-4775, finding F06).

Refines claims are checked on the deterministic trace of each scenario with its own faults, not over every delivery order and fault subset the explorer enumerates: the explorer returns state-invariant verdicts, not steps (WG-4852).
The tree stamp is coarse: any edit of a stamped file makes every evidence result stale until verify runs again, not only the results that depend on it.
The application evaluates claims without current stamps, so every recorded fact is unverifiable there and the claims resting on them read undecided in the application (WG-5688).

A lean-theorem claim is not bound to what its statement says: a theorem that mentions the named code but states nothing about it is still proved; a change of its statement is refused by admit unless a superseding implication exists, but the claim does not pin the statement it expects (WG-5690).
Object and generic types (for example {text, hash} or Operation[]) are opaque to the type check: their values are accepted unchecked.
A response is paired with its request by one correlation field or by count; there is no timeout or ordering rule for unanswered requests at the end of a run.
A field counts as a name when its type text contains the word name or handle; there is no type system for field types, so a party field typed as an opaque string passes rule party-by-id (WG-4697).
Retention is free text: nothing checks that a record's retention and its copies' erasure points agree, and a copy of a copy cannot be declared, since of names records only (WG-4697).

Built (WG-4715, WG-4729): the metric-bound method is registered and evaluated on format-2 scenarios derived from a specification, reporting model-holds, violated or inconclusive with N, the passes, the fraction and the confidence, with negatives and control negatives. Not built: calibration, sensitivity, the operating envelope and revision binding (asOf is only recorded) (planned: WG-4741).

The status model-holds is implemented: it is a ClaimResult status of src/core/claims.js and the verdict of src/core/metric-stats.js, and metric-bound claims report it. Its final name and display follow WG-4703.

The engine itself is not driven: it runs a scenario to quiescence and delivers simultaneous events in queue order, so the replay reimplements one engine step in JavaScript without faults. Agreement with the engine is by construction from the same engine input and expression language, not checked against the Rust engine.
A stream that starts mid-session (after the recorder dropped events, past 5000) is replayed from the declared initial configuration; divergences near its start can come from the missing prefix.

Divergences a longer real session still shows (WG-4782): the camera saved after a view switch with nothing stored is the camera the fit animation produced, not the last camera the model tracked (camera-keep); a restored camera is saved again with its last digit changed by the view's round trip (camera-apply); a commit that changes only comments or formatting re-evaluates no claims, while claims-on-commit predicts an evaluation for every change of the specification text (missing claims-evaluation-requested); a terminated engine worker never finishes its run, while engine-worker-flow still emits worker-run-done for it (missing).
Property access reads top-level properties of entities only: a nested object property such as implementation.status or evaluate.method cannot be addressed (follow-up of WK-396).
Entity ids written as literals in a rule are not references: a rename does not rewrite them and a delete does not see them (follow-up of WK-396).
Undo, redo and reload are not checked by the ratchet: they restore or adopt text that was valid before, and may bring back a violation.
The Lean facts are exported by JavaScript: that they are the specification is checked differentially (exegra-lean integrity against the evaluator), not proved.

Derived relations are evaluated by naive iteration: every candidate tuple of the product of the parameter domains, each clause through the general formula evaluator, with no semi-naive evaluation and no indexing of atoms. Relations above 100000 candidates are refused, and a relation over Exegra's own relationships and components would slow every edit, so Exegra's own specification declares none yet; the examples are in tests/fixtures/integrity/relations.jsonc (WG-5267).
Pages are derived in full on every scene change; a very large kind is cut to the first 300 matching rows on the surface, not paged.

Two differences from the JavaScript parser where Lean strings cannot follow: a lone surrogate in a string becomes U+FFFD before the call, and the label of a declared entity kind is lower-cased in ASCII only in the entity.type and id.missing messages. The JSON reply carries -0 as 0 and a number beyond the double range as null; the parser then takes entity data and the vocabulary from the syntax tree.

Recursion over the document is bounded by fuel (twice the document depth plus 8); no theorem states that the bound is never reached, the differential test (tests/core/model-kernel.test.js) is the evidence that it is not.
The id check implements the pattern ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*(-[a-z0-9_]+)*$ of src/core/metamodel.json in Lean; it does not read idPattern from the meta-model it is given (it only quotes it in the message).

tasks.detail: Known unknown of Semantic hash binding.
tasks.title: Not in the verdict path in the strict sense: a claim's result is stamped with this binding's hash, so a binding error would misstamp a result without changing a verdict. The stamp is compared with the Lean-derived hash only by the callers that use it (for example transactions' expectHash checks).

The search is bounded and its payloads are representative, not exhaustive: a transition reported unreachable within the bound may be reached by a longer sequence or another payload; only the structural case (a source state nothing enters) is certain (WG-4965).
A guard outcome nothing reaches is listed as open in the report, not as a finding; deciding that the outcome is impossible (complementary guards) is left to the reader (WG-4965).

The verified explorer of formal/ (engine.explore) explores the interleavings and fault subsets of one scenario, not sequences of inputs, so the search runs the engine once per sequence instead (WG-4965).

The browser application opens a project without its product files: src/app/session.js builds the Project from the specification alone, and the workspace watcher does not watch product files (follow-up of WG-4989).
Whether a product's claims and scenarios are about its own entities is not checked; any claim or scenario may be declared in a product file.

The product sections are a fixed list in src/core/layers.js and src/core/layer-values.js; nothing yet generates the tenant bundle a product installs through the platform's install-bundle contract. The check does not parse the block text of a template. The scope of an automation's expressions is not known here (the params come from the triggers that start it and the outputs of its steps), so its fields and params are accepted and only its syntax, shapes and roles are checked.

The evaluation of claims is not cached: it runs the verified engine, and a claims run still takes the time of its scenarios after the derivation stages hit. Measured on the Strata specification (about 10,000 entities): validate 13.9 s cold, 1.0 s warm; claims 16.4 s cold, 7.8 s warm.
The diagnostics of a validate hit are rebuilt as copies: their loc objects are equal to the entities' but no longer the same objects. Nothing reads the identity.

Exhaustive exploration results (exegra prove) are not recorded in a project, so a trace claim is reported as explored only when the caller passes them; claims, evaluate, the claims report and admit never do yet (WG-5280).

The value analysis ignores guards when it collects the values and states nominal runs reach and does not follow arithmetic or keyed instances, so vacuity that depends on them is not found; restated-scenario examines only a plain comparison with a literal.

Grounding is structural: an anchored behavior may still branch on a field that means nothing, and the expression language cannot read roles, capabilities or grants, so the access model reaches a behavior only through a contract's auth.requires.
The partial order compares open assumptions as a sublist in declaration order: reordering a claim's assumptions is a move that is not upward, so it is a regression.

The meet of undecided and asserted is refuted, as the order of criterion 1 of WG-5684 forces: a conjunction of an untested part and a part only asserted by a document reads refuted (shown as violated when a fact failed, otherwise not-evaluated), and a part whose only positive fact is stale reads refuted with freshness stale, so that staleness never raises a status and strength only comes from fresh facts.

Test evidence depends on the files its run covered only when verify ran the node test itself; reused outcomes and browser tests record no coverage, a theorem depends on the Exegra constants its statement uses one level deep, and verify --change trusts the entities and files the change set names (WG-5689).

Composition is the concatenation of the machine lists of one engine input; the theorem that it equals the composition of separately elaborated systems (Sys.compose), and that refinement is preserved by composition with a third system, belong to WG-5685.

Engine input and trace format 2 (contracts engine-input-v2 and trace-v2) are derived by the Lean lowering (Exegra.Lower.engineInput) whenever a specification uses a format-2 construct and run by the engine's version-2 semantics (engine/exegra-engine/src/lib.rs dispatches on the version). A specification that uses no format-2 construct still derives version 1, unchanged.

The machines a quota pool runs as are derived, not entities: renaming a pool does not rewrite claim expressions that name them, and the simulator panel and inspector list only declared behaviors (WG-5281).

Exegra.Lower.lower gives a system of the behaviour calculus only for a scenario the elaborator takes (resources, resource faults, routes, keyed instances and measured outputs included since WG-5683); a scenario with links or workloads is LowerError.refused, so engine.run and engine.runScenario still run the lowered engine input through the version-2 dispatch (the legacy interpreter outside the fragment) rather than Exec.runTrace of the lowered system, there is no engine_entry_eq, and the conditions the lowering relies on are not a decidable WellFormed in Lean with lower_ok and per-condition validate codes (WG-5683, criteria 5 to 7).
The engine input (format version 1) carries no bound of a scenario's fault model, so every subset of the scenario's faults is explored; the concurrency bounds of fault models are not applied yet.
A fault acts for the whole run or not at all: a fault without an occurrence cannot act on some deliveries of its event and not on others.
Breadth-first order makes a counterexample one of the fewest steps, but that is not proved.
The Rust explorer for large state spaces is not built yet (planned: WG-4650); it will be checked differentially against this one.

Format 2 inputs are not explored yet (planned: WG-4664, WG-4715). The specified relation adds internal entries to the simultaneous-order choice, the new fault kinds to the mask, and one successor per choice value and per instance of an any route; sampled draws are fixed by a seed named first in the result, and a result is shown as verified only when the scenario has no sampled site. Scenarios with workloads need a short horizon and maxArrivals, and keyed populations of thousands of clients are beyond reach. When a timed fault acts is not explored (WG-4704).
Temporal claims are checked without the claim's negatives and without the trace check's vacuity rules (a never whose matcher cannot occur in the scenario holds here without a note).
A violating prefix of a never or precedes claim is reported as the counterexample, not extended to a complete run; any extension violates it too, but that is not a theorem.
A configuration whose invariant cannot be evaluated counts as a violation, and a failed step leads to the error state, which has no successor and violates every invariant.
Strong fairness is not checked: a liveness claim citing a fairness assumption of kind strong is reported not supported.
FG liveness claims are decided only by refutation (a weakly fair lasso); no proof rule for FG is implemented, so an FG claim with no lasso is reported not supported.

The ranking search assigns ranks backwards from the states that satisfy the property; when a step other than the helpful one raises the rank, checkRanking fails and a GF claim that holds is reported not supported.

Liveness is checked over every run, Zeno runs included. On a finite state space every cycle keeps the time, so every lasso with a step of the relation is a Zeno run and is reported as one; liveness over non-Zeno runs only (NonZeno) is not checked, and a scenario whose time grows without bound has infinitely many states, so its liveness claims are incomplete.
Fairness is per label: with sampled delays every (entry, draws) label is its own action, a stronger assumption than fairness per entry; without sampled delays a label is its entry.
The attempt cap (Cfg.attCap) is argued, not proved, to give the same fault matches as format 2's unbounded attempt counts: no theorem relates the two.
exegra prove does not search for k-inductive strengthenings; kInduction_sound is used only in hand-written proofs.

Format 2 is defined in formal/Exegra/Format2.lean for the constructs built so far (instances, routes, resources and resource faults, windows, workloads, links, timers, request lifecycle and measured outputs); formal/Exegra/Resource.lean proves the held-units and queue-bound invariants of a settled resource, the strict FIFO queue of a collapse included. Not defined yet: crash-instance with incarnations, meters and cost (planned: WG-4741).
The determinism property over seeds is not stated as a theorem for format 2 yet (planned: WG-4741).

Exegra.Json.parse is a partial definition, shared by the definition and the implementation, so it is outside every theorem (planned: WG-4797). Inputs outside the behaviour calculus run the legacy format-2 interpreter, which parses each expression at every evaluation (planned: WG-4798).
The guarded-command calculus (Calculus.lean) is single-sorted (Int) with no events, timers, faults or time.

The behaviour calculus (Behav.lean, BehavExec.lean, BehavRename.lean, BehavCheck.lean, BehavRes.lean) covers resources, resource faults, routes and keyed instances, and inputs that measure outputs run on it (metrics are a function of the trace) (WG-5683: a world of holdings, waiting lists and acting resource faults, use/acquire/release as phase-2 operations settled after phase 2 in machine order under the resource as the acting faults leave it, service-done, wait-timeout and fault-edge entries, world draws checked against the settling's holes; a keyed behaviour as slot machines that routes make live, routes decided when an entry is first delivered, before faults act, with random routes as the first world draws of the step; Ref.one, Ref.uniq and Ref.key for single-instance reads, format 2's resolve-before-evaluate ambiguity and the instance key), but not links, workloads, option types or a scenario step addressed to an instance of a keyed behaviour. Elab.elab refuses inputs that use them as outOfFragment; they keep running on the legacy format-2 interpreter (Exegra.V2.traceOf), which computes on exact rationals, their trace says "semantics": "legacy", and no theorem is about them (WG-5683, criteria 1 to 3: the calculus is to cover them, outOfFragment and the legacy V2.step and traceOf are then deleted).

The calculus explorer's temporal check reads the format-2 encoding of each step (ProveB.lean, Occ) to match occurrences; that encoding is shared with traceOfB but no theorem relates a matched occurrence to the calculus label of the step.

Some format-2 values are errors in the calculus: untyped arithmetic with an operand or result outside 2^53 - 1, == and != across sorts (refused as ill-typed), mixed string and number +, and a payload field read at a sort it does not fit; > and >= are encoded as swapped < and <= (which error is reported can change), and the error reported can depend on the order of the winners. The legacy interpreter reports the same errors for elaborated inputs (differential.js --calculus); the Rust oracle computes untyped numbers as doubles and differs on non-integer arithmetic (tests/conformance/expected-differences.json).
Faults are chosen all-or-nothing per fault (one mask per run), not per occurrence. There are no traces, observations, fairness or composition yet (milestones M5 and M6), and no k-induction (M4).

The calculus explorer that exegra prove runs uses Gen.search, whose visited set hashes with an opaque hash, so a generated proof file discharges its verdict with native_decide and trusts the compiler. The list-based Gen.searchL returns the same result (search_eq_searchL) and reduces in the kernel (Exec.cex_refutesL, Exec.holds_invariantL), but its membership test is linear in the visited states, so generated proof files do not use it.
Semantic completeness (invariant_iff_exists_inductive) is over arbitrary predicates; inductive invariants expressible in the calculus's expressions need not exist.

invariant_rename is stated for systems without resources and without routes (hres : sys.resources = [], hroutes : sys.routes = []): renaming does not yet carry the owners of resource holdings, waiting requests and service-done entries, and a least-busy route reads those owners (WG-5683).

A calculus request id comes from a counter in the world (World.nextReq), so the state space of a system with resources is infinite unless the run is bounded; closed-set certificates (exegra prove --module) do not close for such systems (WG-5683).

Results are established by native_decide, so each theorem of a generated proof file depends on an auxiliary axiom that trusts the Lean compiler and runtime. Only the modules exegra prove --module writes are checked by the kernel alone (decide), and only for state-invariant claims that hold; that the system such a module writes out is the elaboration of the scenario rests on the generator (Exegra.V2.ProveKernel.kernelModule), not on a theorem.

Claim results are reported by exegra prove only; evaluate and verify do not show them, except that a state-invariant claim naming the theorem of a committed module (evaluate.theorem) reads proved when Lean accepts it.
Negatives of a claim are not explored in Lean: prove checks that a claim holds on every configuration of its scenarios, not that its negatives violate it (WG-4711).

Built (WG-4664, WG-4729) in the Lean semantics and the Rust engine, resource faults included (set-capacity, set-class-limit, collapse-classes, scale-demand, replace-demand; untimed, or windowed through fault-edge steps), and derived from a specification's resources by simulationInput. crash-instance with incarnations is refused by both engines, and the grantable-units check is not repeated after the untimed fault mask (planned: WG-4741).
Processor sharing is not part of format 2; CPU is a FCFS multi-server station (planned: WG-4719).
Credit-based backpressure between components is not represented (planned: WG-4722); autoscaling and cold start are not represented (planned: WG-4720).

Built (WG-4715, WG-4729): open, closed and population workloads, address groups, links (bandwidth, ordering, queue bounds, fan-out, latency) and timers in both engines, derived from a specification's workloads and links by the Lean lowering (Exegra.Lower.engineInput, WG-5683).
Packet-level networking and packet-rate floods are not represented: a link is a FIFO byte pipe with a latency distribution, one step per message (aggregated mode planned: WG-4718).
Matchmaking gather is writable only as a hand-written behavior (primitive planned: WG-4721).

Built (WG-4715, WG-4729): resource metrics; request classes with the request lifecycle, response time, outcomes, throughput, legitimate refusals (false positives) and transition firings, over the window and per series bucket, in both engines. Not built: link and cost metrics, waiting time per class, resource signals per bucket, time-to-first and time-to-recover, meters, and truncation by an open measured request (planned: WG-4741). Warm-up is declared, not detected.
